title: Eval change delta tracing and alert attenuation for Console alerting
creator: Lars Nguyen
description: Build a Console-first eval alerting flow that ties quality regressions to the originating config or model change and reduces noisy duplicate alerts across related evals. The feature should: (1) surface a clear change -> eval delta trace in the alert payload and dashboard, (2) attenuate duplicate signals across similar evaluation suites and related checkpoints, and (3) provide deterministic routing for Slack and PagerDuty with configurable suppression windows for rollouts/canaries.
acceptance_criteria: Console alert payload includes the change fingerprint (commit/model-id/config-id), the affected eval metric delta, and a short list of top contributing testcases
Alerts posted to Slack and PagerDuty include a stable fingerprint enabling downstream dedupe (same fingerprint dedupes for N minutes configurable)
UI shows a time-series 'delta trace' linking the model/config change event to subsequent eval score regressions with root-cause hints
Canary/rollout-aware suppression exists: alerts from canary cohorts are rate-limited and flagged, not dropped, and have an override option
Attenuation algorithm groups related evals (by prompt family, metric, or dataset) and emits a single summarized alert with links to grouped eval IDs
Documentation and runbook exist outlining how on-call should interpret the fingerprint, and how to acknowledge/suppress grouped alerts
End-to-end test exists that simulates a model rollout causing a regression across 5 related evals and validates one grouped alert is emitted to Slack and a single PagerDuty incident is created

discussion: 2025-02-14 Lars Nguyen: Kickoff — goal is to reduce noisy PagerDuty incidents caused by repeated regressions across similar eval suites. We should preserve signal fidelity for triage.
2025-02-18 Amira Patel: Proposed attenuation heuristic — group evals by prompt family and metric, compute weighted delta, emit grouped alert if > threshold. Will ask Eng to validate cost.

2025-02-20 Priya Rao (Eng): Backend design reviewed — we will create a change_fingerprint table keyed by (model_hash|config_hash|rollout_id) and attach fingerprint to eval-run telemetry. Proof-of-concept PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6241

2025-02-22 UX review: Small inline card vs modal for delta trace. Decided on inline expandable card in alert stream to avoid context switching. See Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/eval-delta-trace
2025-02-25 Security: No secrets in alerts. Confirmed fingerprint is opaque hash. Security OK on that basis.
2025-02-27 QA: E2E harness created and failing in edge case where two independent changes produce same metric delta. Need collision-resistant fingerprinting (include timestamp and rollout_id).
decisions: Use combined fingerprint: sha256(model_hash + '|' + config_hash + '|' + rollout_id + '|' + truncated_timestamp)
Attenuation window default: 15 minutes for Slack, 30 minutes for PagerDuty; configurable per project
Grouped alert contains top 5 contributing evals, aggregated delta, and direct links to eval detail pages
Canary suppression mode will set severity to 'warning' and route to a separate on-call rotation unless manually promoted
risks: False grouping: unrelated evals may be aggregated if heuristics are too loose
Latency: additional mapping step could add ~50-100ms to eval result path if not optimized
PagerDuty dedupe depends on remote integration behavior; may require vendor-specific headers
Operational complexity: on-call needs training on grouped alerts and fingerprint semantics
